candidates.attacker_control: The interlace-method byte is the last data byte of the 13-byte IHDR chunk in the PNG file, fully attacker-controlled, together with the rest of the file. No privilege or unusual parameter is needed: the file just has to be offered to a library read API (e.g. Imaging.getImageInfo(byte[])/getImageSize/getBufferedImage, or the corresponding ImageParser methods) that inspects untrusted images.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Confirmed readByte returns a signed byte (BinaryFunctions.java:74-81), so 0x80-0xFF become negative ints; confirmed InterlaceMethod has only NONE and ADAM7 (InterlaceMethod.java:24-38); confirmed the two `&&` clauses are mutually exclusive for every int value, i.e. the guard is provably dead; confirmed the enum result is used without a null/range-returning lookup (contrast PngColorType.getColorType, which returns null for unknown values and is properly checked in the same constructor at lines 46-49); confirmed no RuntimeException handling in the call path and no earlier interlace validation elsewhere in PngImageParser; confirmed the same chunk path is used by several public APIs. Not verified at runtime (no execution allowed), and I did not consult upstream history/patches, so I cannot claim a fix commit or CVE mapping.
candidates.impact: Denial of service / unexpected crash in applications that parse untrusted PNG data: a single-byte modification of an otherwise valid PNG makes a routine read call throw an uncaught ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. Callers that only handle the declared ImageReadException/IOException (the library's documented failure mode) will experience request/thread failure or application-level error handling bypass. Because Java is memory-safe, no memory corruption or code execution results; the impact is availability and robustness of image-processing services.
candidates.prerequisites: Caller parses an attacker-supplied PNG through a public Imaging/ImageParser read path. A valid 8-byte PNG signature plus a syntactically parseable IHDR chunk is required; the IHDR 'interlace method' byte must be any value other than 0 or 1 (values 2-127 index past the 2-entry enum, values 128-255 sign-extend to negative indices). No other condition is needed.
candidates.root_cause: PngChunkIhdr reads the 1-byte IHDR interlace method with readByte(...) (signed byte, line 52) and validates it with `if (method < 0 && method >= InterlaceMethod.values().length)` (line 53). Both clauses cannot be true simultaneously, so the guard never fires. `InterlaceMethod.values()` has exactly two constants (InterlaceMethod.java lines 26-27), so any method value other than 0 or 1 (including negative values for raw bytes >= 0x80) is dereferenced at line 56 and throws an unchecked ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. The intended check was almost certainly `||`.
candidates.title: Dead interlace-method validation in PngChunkIhdr allows out-of-bounds enum index (unchecked ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException on crafted PNG)
candidates.trace: Imaging.getImageInfo(byte[]) (Imaging.java:633) -> PngImageParser.getImageInfo(ByteSource,...) requests ChunkType.IHDR (PngImageParser.java:328-337) -> PngImageParser.readChunks(...) (line 148) reads length/type/data -> new PngChunkIhdr(length, chunkType, crc, bytes) (line 185-186) -> readByte("InterlaceMethod",...) returns the attacker byte (line 52) -> the `&&` check at line 53 is always false -> InterlaceMethod.values()[method] (line 56) throws java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. There is no catch of RuntimeException in PngImageParser/Imaging (verified no `catch (` blocks in those files), so the unchecked exception escapes instead of the declared ImageReadException/IOException, aborting the caller's parsing operation. The same constructor is reached by getImageSize (PngImageParser.java:256-270) and getBufferedImage (PngImageParser.java:490-509).
candidates.unverified: The exception was not executed or fuzzed (no code execution permitted), so the exact index value and stack trace are inferred from source only. I also did not verify whether upstream later changed `&&` to `||` (no git history or network available); the candidate is a source-evidenced defect claim, not a runtime-confirmed or patch-confirmed vulnerability.
candidates.weakness_type: Improper validation of attacker-controlled index/offset (CWE-1285/CWE-129) leading to unchecked ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException (availability impact)

coverage_summary: Coverage: 375 model-visible files (parity note: same filters for B0/P1); source root contains main Java sources under src/main/java plus build/config/site files, and no test sources were exposed. I read or searched the major parsing paths: PNG (chunk loop, IHDR/PLTE/text/ICC/transparency/scanline code), GIF (header, image descriptor, LZW decompressor), JPEG (segment walking, DHT/SOF/SOS, decoder, IPTC), TIFF (reader/directory/field types, strip/tile data readers, CCITT G3/G4), BMP (headers plus RGB/bitfield/RLE pixel parsers), PCX/DCX RLE, PSD, PNM, RGBE/HDR, ICNS/ICO, WBMP, XBM/XPM, ICC profile parser, BinaryFunctions/ByteSource helpers and the public Imaging API. I could not execute code, fuzz, diff against upstream history, or inspect tests; findings are source-level only, and the review is not exhaustive for every writer path or every helper (e.g., ICNS/ICO/PSD internals and writer-side code were skimmed rather than fully audited).
limitations: No execution, tests, fuzzing, or static-analysis tooling was available; all findings are inferred from reading source, so no runtime confirmation of the crash or of exploitability is claimed.

No git history, patches, CVE/CWE mappings, or upstream comparisons were available, so I cannot confirm which later upstream fix corresponds to this snapshot; the candidate is a lead, not a confirmed or patch-verified vulnerability.
The visible scope is source-only (375 files, no tests and no dependency jars), so behavior reachable only through tests, examples, or external callers was not inspected.
Java's memory safety means the strongest issues here are availability bugs (unchecked exceptions, infinite loops, unbounded allocations); no memory-corruption or code-execution impact is claimed.
Some files were skimmed rather than line-by-line reviewed (e.g., ICO/ICNS/PSD readers, ICC tag parsing details, and writer paths), so additional defects may exist that are not listed.

rejected_leads.lead: MyLzwDecompressor.initializeTable: `final int intialEntriesCount = 1 << codeSize + 2;` (precedence bug; intended `(1 << codeSize) + 2`) initializes up to 4x the legal entries; for a GIF LZW minimum code size byte >= 11 it indexes past the 4096-entry table and throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException (MyLzwDecompressor.java lines 66-74, reached from GifImageParser.readImageDescriptor line 388-397).
rejected_leads.reason: Real and attacker-triggerable, but rejected only because of the one-candidate cap and because it requires a malformed GIF LZW code-size byte (normally 2-8) rather than a nearly valid file; the PNG IHDR defect has a provably dead validation check and broader reachability.

rejected_leads.lead: RgbeInfo.decompress: the RLE loop lacks EOF/overflow handling (`out[position++]` unbounded, and `in.read()` returning -1 yields n=-1 so the while(position<total) loop spins forever), giving an infinite-loop CPU DoS and possible ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException when decoding a truncated/crafted HDR image (RgbeInfo.java lines 171-191, called from getPixelData line 148 / RgbeImageParser.getBufferedImage line 103).
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible and potentially severe (hang rather than exception), but kept as a rejected lead under the single-candidate cap; no runtime confirmation and only the full-decode path reaches it.

rejected_leads.lead: T4AndT6Compression: decompressT4_2D writes referenceLine[rowLength + i] and fillRange writes referenceRow[i] without clamping to `width` (lines 441-444 and 700-706), so crafted CCITT G3-2D/G4 TIFF data can index past the row array.
rejected_leads.reason: Real-looking bounds gap in TIFF fax decoding, but needs a crafted TIFF/G3-2D/G4 stream and was not selected over the PNG finding.

rejected_leads.lead: PngImageParser.readChunks uses the file-supplied 4-byte chunk length with no validation before readBytes(...), which does `new byte[length]` (BinaryFunctions.java:89-104); huge lengths cause OutOfMemoryError and negative lengths cause NegativeArraySizeException (PngImageParser.java lines 153-168).
rejected_leads.reason: Classic unchecked-allocation DoS, but very common library behavior and less specific than the dead validation; not selected under the one-candidate cap.

rejected_leads.lead: PNG text/ICC chunk constructors index bytes without checking the minimum chunk length (PngChunkItxt.java lines 60/69/74, PngChunkZtxt.java line 49, PngChunkIccp.java line 60), allowing AIOOBE/NegativeArraySizeException from very short crafted chunks; RgbeInfo's FORMAT check compares `value` instead of `variable` (RgbeInfo.java lines 116-117), defeating that validation.
rejected_leads.reason: All plausible but secondary, unconfirmed as fixed/known issues, and omitted to keep a single strongest candidate.

summary: Reviewed the Apache Commons Imaging 1.0-SNAPSHOT source tree (375 visible files; all main Java sources, build/config/site files; no tests were exposed). I traced untrusted-image parsing paths across PNG, GIF, JPEG, TIFF, BMP, PCX/DCX, PSD, PNM, RGBE, ICNS/ICO, WBMP, XBM/XPM and the ICC/LZW/CCITT helpers. The strongest single, distinct candidate is in the PNG IHDR chunk parser: PngChunkIhdr.java line 53 contains a logically impossible validation condition (`method < 0 && method >= InterlaceMethod.values().length`). Because the two clauses can never both hold, the intended rejection of an invalid interlace-method byte is dead code, and the raw, attacker-controlled byte is used directly to index `InterlaceMethod.values()` one line later. Any PNG whose IHDR interlace byte is anything other than 0 or 1 (e.g. 0x02–0x7F, or 0x80–0xFF which sign-extends to a negative index) throws an uncaught ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException from ordinary public read APIs (Imaging.getImageSize/getImageInfo/getBufferedImage), i.e. an easily triggered denial-of-service / unexpected RuntimeException in place of the intended ImageReadException. Java's memory safety limits the direct impact to availability, but the defect is unambiguous at source level.
